---
title: "RADB sites Exploration"
code-fold: true
---

Purpose: explore RADB's `sites` table with a view to harmonisation.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(DBI)
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)
library(here)

here::i_am("docs/radb-sites.qmd")

# requres RPostgres to be built + installed
# which in turn requres PSQL to be installed

# read in project-specific renviron
readRenviron(here::here(".Renviron"))

# Check renviron variables exist
pg_sysenv <- Sys.getenv(c(
  "PGHOST",
  "PGPORT",
  "PGDATABASE",
  "PGUSER",
  "PGPASSWORD"
))

# check all exist
stopifnot(!("" %in% pg_sysenv))
# assign in environment
list2env(as.list(pg_sysenv), envir = globalenv())

con <- dbConnect(
  RPostgres::Postgres(),
  dbname = PGDATABASE,
  host = PGHOST,
  port = PGPORT,
  user = PGUSER,
  password = PGPASSWORD
)

set.seed(123)

## Functions ##
sample_n_safe <- function(x, n) {
  x_unique <- unique(x)
  x_unique[sample.int(length(x_unique), min(n, length(x_unique)))]
}

classify_value <- function(x) {
  recode_values(x, c(NA, NULL) ~ "NA or NULL", 0 ~ "0", default = ">0")
}

read_or_write_parquet <- function(con, table_name, file_name) {
  if (!file.exists(file_name)) {
    table <- dbGetQuery(
      con,
      glue::glue("SELECT * FROM {table_name};")
    )
    nanoparquet::write_parquet(
      table,
      file_name
    )
  } else {
    table <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(
      file_name
    )
  }
  table
}

kable_abbreviate <- function(x, n) {
  table <- slice_head(x, n = n) |> knitr::kable()
  nrows <- nrow(x)
  print(table)
  if (nrows > n) {
    print(glue("\n\n*and {nrows - n} more rows*"))
  }
}

kable_glimpse <- function(x, n = 20, width = 40) {
  summary <- tibble(
    name = names(x),
    type = vapply(x, \(col) class(col)[1], character(1)),
    n_na = vapply(x, \(col) sum(is.na(col)), integer(1)),
    n_distinct = vapply(x, n_distinct, integer(1)),
    examples = vapply(
      x,
      \(col) {
        sample_n_safe(col[!is.na(col)], n) |>
          as.character() |>
          # \r escape in some comments needs to be removed
          str_replace(pattern = "\\r", replacement = "") |>
          str_trunc(width) |>
          str_flatten_comma()
      },
      character(1)
    )
  )
  cat(glue("{ncol(x)} cols x {nrow(x)} rows\n\n"))
  print(knitr::kable(summary))
}
```


# `sites`

```{r}
#| label: load-tables

sites <- read_or_write_parquet(
  con,
  "sites",
  here::here("data", "sites.parquet")
)

environmental_con <- read_or_write_parquet(
  con,
  "environmental_con",
  here::here("data", "environmental_con.parquet")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: sites-glimpse
sites |> kable_glimpse()
```

- There are quite a lot of sites in RADB
- A few issues related to data integrity to check first:

## `sites` data integrity check

### unique IDs

- Do all sites have a unique `site_id`, `site_code`, `site_name`?

```{r}
#| label: sites-ids

id_all_unique <- function(table, col) {
  all(count(table, {{ col }}, sort = TRUE) |> pull(n) == 1)
}

id_all_unique(sites, site_id)
id_all_unique(sites, site_code)
id_all_unique(sites, site_name)
```

- Site names aren't unique, which is not an issue as they're not expected to be

### sites in `environmental-con`

- Do all sites correspond to at least one sample from `environmental-con`:

```{r}
#| label: sites-all-in-env-con

anti_join(sites, environmental_con, by = join_by(site_code)) |>
  kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

- We can see from the above that no, 28,942 sites aren't in `environmental-con`
- This is not immediately a problem, but we can see that some `site_code` are corrupted (e.g. `S3-VÃ˜YENBEKKEN`)
- More details below

## `site_id`

```{r}
#| label: site-id-summary
sites |> count(site_id, sort = TRUE) |> kable_abbreviate(n = 20)
```

- eData doesn't have a `site_id` column, as it's assumed this would be set on RADB upload

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- None.

**Assessment**

- Priority: 0/5
- Difficulty: 0/5
:::

## `site_code`

```{r}
#| label: site-code-types
site_code_types <- sites |>
  count(site_code, site_name) |>
  mutate(
    site_code_type = case_when(
      str_detect(site_code, "[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{5,6}") ~ "Vm Freshwater",
      str_detect(site_code, "HAV-[0-9]{5}") ~ "Vm Ocean",
      str_detect(site_code, "[0-9]{2}\\.[0-9]{2}-[0-9]+") ~ "Vm Transitional",
      str_detect(site_code, "^J") ~ "JOVA?",
      .default = "Other"
    )
  )

site_code_types |>
  group_by(site_code_type) |>
  reframe(codes_sample = str_flatten_comma(sample_n_safe(site_code, n = 10))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

- RADB doesn't appear to have any strict constraints on `site_code`
- since `environmental_con` contains both `site_code` and `site_id`, I presume that the tables join on `site_id`, which means that `site_code` doesn't strictly need to be unique
- nevertheless, the current `site_code` variables are all unique
- eData generates a [Sites - SITE_CODE](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/sites_data.html#site-code---string-free-mandatory) based on campaign, long form site name, and a serial number. This isn't necessarily a better option, but it might be good to lay down some "principles of a good site_code"

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- No changes immediately needed for harmonisation between schemes
- Review guidelines for site codes if needed

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 1/5
:::

## `site_name`

```{r}
#| label: site-name-summary
site_code_types |>
  group_by(site_code_type) |>
  reframe(names_sample = str_flatten_comma(sample_n_safe(site_name, n = 10))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

- Site names are presumably also based on original site names
- Using site names is difficult - they often make sense only in the immediate context of the study
- In general, assigning names to arbitrary spatial points (reverse geocoding) is difficult, but this spatial information is often very important for interpreting data
- If users search data by site name, collisions between names may be an issue?
- How does one e.g. get all data for a specific county? 
- eData doesn't solve any of these problems either


::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Review geodata needs of database
- Consider developing guidelines for naming sites depending on needs

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 5/5
:::

## `country`

```{r}
sites |> count(country) |> knitr::kable()
```

- Countries are a mix of two-letter codes (ISO-3166-A2?) and names
- I believe `country` is a mandatory field in some versions of the input spreadsheet, but not all sites will be in countries (or indeed on land)
- Out of interest, which sites have no country code?

```{r}
sites |> filter(is.na(country)) |> kable_abbreviate(n = 25)
```

- Some of these are chemical inventories, some appear to be "orphan" sites without relevant information
- eData [Sites - COUNTRY_ISO](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/sites_data.html#iso-country---string-controlled-mandatory) standardises to ISO-3166 country names. I recommend this over two-letter codes, as some of the latter aren't obvious (e.g. `HR` for Croatia)

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Set format (ISO-3166 names?) and harmonise data
- Enforce format in Db and applications
- Review orphan sites and remove if necessary
- Consider adding new column for ocean sites, based on eData [Sites - OCEAN_IHO](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/sites_data.html#iho-oceansea---string-controlled-mandatory)

**Assessment**

- Priority: 2/5
- Difficulty: 2/5
:::

## `area`

```{r}
sites |> count(area) |> knitr::kable()
```

- Very useful to capture lower-level geographical information, but `area` doesn't enforce any formatting, so difficult to use
- Alternatively, possible to reverse-geocode based on coordinate data, which may be a better solution (could be done on-demand in STOPredictor?)

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Review geographical needs for data and determine most pragmatic solution
- Standardise based on [NUTS](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/nuts) (Europe-only) and/or FAO's [Global Administrative Unit Layers](https://openknowledge.fao.org/items/aebf0333-a0e3-4177-9d4a-bb2472d0367e)?

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 3/5
:::

## Coordinates

### `coordinate_system`

```{r}
sites |> count(coordinate_system) |> knitr::kable()
```

- Most sites use `WGS 84`, but there doesn't appear to be a table for controlled CRS vocabulary
- Some errors (`WGS 83`, `WGS1984 UTM Zone 32N` - should be `ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N`)
- eData uses full ESPG dataset ([Sites - SITE_COORDINATE_SYSTEM](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/sites_data.html#coordinate-reference-system---string-controlled-mandatory)) of CRS then highlights to those relevant to Arctic

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Recommend use of eData solution as vocabulary table for consistency with ESPG
- Check CRS in existing data are valid
- Add constraints that all sites with lat/long must have CRS

**Assessment**

- Priority: 2/5
- Difficulty: 3/5

:::

### `latitude` and `longitude`

```{r}
sites_wgs84 <- sites |>
  filter(coordinate_system == "WGS 84") |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = rnaturalearth::countries110) +
  geom_sf(data = sites_wgs84, aes(geometry = geometry, colour = country)) +
  coord_sf()
```

- Location appears to be correct for most sites, although some `NO` sites appear to be located at 0,0 and of coast of Russia

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Review db sites data for inconsistencies
- Consider adding automated checking at data ingress for whether coordinates are reasonably for selected CRS/country/area/etc.

**Assessment**

- Priority: 2/5
- Difficulty: 3/5
:::


## Altitude

### `altitude_value` and `altitude_unit`

```{r}
sites |> count(classify_value(altitude_value), altitude_unit) |> knitr::kable()
```

- altitude values/units appear to be consistent
- eData's implementation is very similar ([Sites - ALTITUDE_VALUE](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/sites_data.html#altitude-value---numeric-free-mandatory))

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Add guidelines for altitude, including edge cases and cases where altitude not reported

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 1/5
:::

## Provenance and entry metadata

### `entered_by` and `entered_date`

```{r}
sites |> count(entered_by, entered_date, sort = TRUE)
```

- All dates properly formatted
- Identical to eData [Sites - ENTERED_BY](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/sites_data.html#entered-by---string-free-mandatory)

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Consider automating `entered_by` info with STOP user accounts (partially implemented in eData pp)

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 1/5
:::

### `comments`

```{r}
sites |> count(comments, sort = TRUE)
```

- Similar carriage return (`\r`) issue as in other comments fields
- in eData, renamed to [Sites - SITE_COMMENT](https://nivanorge.github.io/eDataDRF/articles/sites_data.html#site-comment---string-free-optional) for clarity

::: {.callout-important title="Recommendations"}

- Add guidance on relevant information for comments

**Assessment**

- Priority: 1/5
- Difficulty: 1/5
:::
